candidates.statement: If V and W are closed braid representatives of knots V and W, and if X = V#W represents V#W, we say that X is the braid connected sum of V and W if there is a 2-sphere in 3-space which intersects X twice and intersects the axis twice, separating the closed braids V and W. We stated in §1 that our proof of Theorem 1 would show that X3 is obtained from X 1 by taking the braid connected sum of X, with some number of closed braid representatives of the unknot UW, say Uj,...,Ux. We have, indeed, shown that there are closed representatives U;,...,U, of the unknot and that X3 = X1#Ui#---#U,, but braid connected sum seems like a stronger assertion. H

In our proof of Theorem 1 we only treated the case of knots, but the proof works equally well for links. A detailed discussion of the case of links (and of many other aspects of the construction given here) will appear in the forthcoming manuscript [7].
